for the $12.5B Longtail development offshore Guyana following government and regulatory approvals.

Longtail, the eighth development located in the southeastern portion of the Stabroek block, marks a new phase of development on the block, targeting non-associated gas and condensate-rich reservoirs, the company said.

The project will utilize a floating production storage and offloading vessel designed to process 1.2B scf/day of gas and produce up to 250K bbl/day of condensate and is expected to include ~45 subsea production and injection wells; it is scheduled to come online in 2030.
said it is producing ~900K bbl/day of oil from four projects in the Stabroek block, which is expected to exceed 1M bbl/day when the fifth project, Uaru, is expected to start production in Q4.
Construction is progressing on two additional approved projects: Whiptail, expected to begin production in 2027, and Hammerhead, expected to follow in 2029.
is the Longtail operator and holds a 45% interest in the Stabroek block, while partners Hess and Cnooc hold 30% and 25% interests, respectively.

title: Exxon approves $12.5B Longtail project offshore Guyana
